newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Bunds to falter, core support at 102.60.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Bunds to falter, core support at 102.60.

text.p: September Bund futures on LIFFE look vulnerable and are likely to target a key area of support around 102.60, technical analysts said on Friday.
"Bunds are looking very, very hesitant after trading in a tiny range yesterday and closing relatively weakly," said Elli Gifford, independent technical analyst near Cambridge.
"This suggests they have seen some of their highs for now."
The Bund contract traded a 102.95-103.48 range on Thursday, and closed at 103.05.
September was trading at 102.98 at 0647 GMT, down seven basis points on the day.
"The 102.60 level is a core of support from the range before we reached the new highs, it is not a specific number in its own right," said Gifford.
The contract high of 103.52 reached on Wednesday remains key resistance for Friday's session, but the market is unlikely to make it there, Gifford said.
"There is non-confirmation from several indicators of that high."
Nearer resistance lies at 103.30, Gifford said, and 103.00 also provides a top, although the contract edged through there in early trade.
Richard Adcock, manager, technical research, at HSBC Futures in London, saw risks of a fall below 102.50.
"The market must rally quickly to establish the bullish picture again, otherwise tests of the supports under 102.50 can be expected," he said in a client note.
"We stay with stops at 102.90, going short on penetrations of...102.86," he added.

December Euromarks were one basis point lower at 96.53 at 0657 GMT. "Rallies are set to struggle now up to 96.59 where further selling opportunities will be offered again. Targets will then be set at 96.45," Adcock said.
